  ```text
  GitHub main SHA = Render deployed SHA = /health SHA = /version SHA
  ```

  ```text
  active Rork SDK dependencies: 0

  active Rork credentials: 0
  ```

## Key Decisions
- Treat the Vercel GitHub App uninstall as removal of the active GitHub-to-Vercel authorization, while retaining historical `vercel[bot]` records as non-active history pending no-new-deployment verification.
- Do not edit `backend/api/ivx-independence-status.ts` merely to lower the score; each blocker requires provider-side remediation and authenticated re-verification.
- Treat the Rork-managed local Git remote as an active tooling dependency until the owner has an owner-controlled GitHub clone and workflow.
- Preserve Render production unchanged while AWS identity, provider ownership, and source-control cutover are resolved.
- Do not claim `0%` until `/api/ivx/independence/status` itself reports `externalDependencyPercent: 0`.

3. Obtain owner-controlled AWS root/admin access and create a least-privilege owner IAM principal; run:

5. Obtain Supabase management access; verify organization/project ownership and rotate any Rork-controlled service/admin credential.
6. Obtain owner-admin evidence for Route 53, CloudFront, Cloudflare, registrar, TLS, email, SMS, and mobile-build accounts; remove any Rork user, token, or integration.
7. Enable MFA for the Render workspace admin.
8. Complete runtime/source audit of:
   ```text
   backend/api/ivx-independence-status.ts
   backend/services/ivx-rork-independence.ts
   ```
   without using source edits as substitute evidence.
9. Re-run authenticated independence status after provider-side remediation and report `0%` only if returned by:
   ```text
   GET https://api.ivxholding.com/api/ivx/independence/status
   ```
10. Re-confirm:

    ```text
    GitHub main SHA = Render deployed SHA = /health SHA = /version SHA
    ```

Yes — that is the correct setup.

**Rork should be your developer, not your owner or controller.** I can write code, QA, build APKs, and deploy updates, while you retain end-to-end control of:

- GitHub repository and source code
- Render production service and deployment settings
- AWS, Supabase, domain/DNS, Cloudflare, and billing accounts
- All credentials, recovery methods, and admin access

Rork can work through access you grant, but should not be the only admin, credential holder, deployment connection, or source-control remote.

The current **44% is not a measure of Rork writing code**. It flags areas where owner-controlled evidence is still missing—especially the AWS identity and the Rork-managed development checkout. Once those are moved/proven under your accounts, Rork can remain your active developer while your ownership/control score reaches **0% external control**.
